reason: Code-only review of the verify-people-site.mjs delta and the supplied people-certified-site, people-site, people-qualified-scope, and native test code. Before the change, verifyPeopleSite called loadPeopleSiteContext({allowMissing:false, allowPreview:false}). With both files present, that returns the unmodified loadCertifiedPeopleSite() result (preview:false), and it then called assertPeopleSiteCertificate, which runs loadCertifiedPeopleSite again with expectedInputs pinned to certificate.inputs and discarded the result. After the change, the artifact checks use the fresh context returned by assertPeopleSiteCertificate, which is the same full loadQualifiedPeopleScope pipeline. That pipeline covers: the identity seal against current inputs, config and prompt-version consistency, per-chapter validation plus extraction, editorial, date-audit, and identity gates, full current-source identity validation, projection, the post-projection evidence recheck, and the expected-input pin. It returns only after the stableJson certificate equality holds. Every downstream check (status counts and generatedAt, publication mode and counts, preview and noindex handling, shard certification inputs and projection, family, chronology, alias, redirect, search, and chapter-link checks, and links outside the certified scope) reads catalog, siteIndex, and certificate from this certified fresh context, so no gate is weakened and the stored certificate stays evidence, not authority. The missing-status branch still calls loadPeopleSiteContext({allowMissing:false, allowPreview:false}) first, so inactive gating and stale-index detection are unchanged, and an active source without status still throws. Edge cases fail closed. An absent or null status.certificate gives expectedInputs undefined, which throws the stale-pin error inside loadQualifiedPeopleScope. Missing catalog or site-index files throw from the readers rather than from the old 'Missing generated people data' message. A forged projection or inputs field is rejected before any artifact check, and the new native test covers the projection case. One accepted change in behaviour: a forged or stale certificate now throws immediately instead of after the status-count assertions are accumulated, which is stricter. No cache, input retagging, or source-data change is present. Limitations: I did not run the tests; I relied on the supplied log of 2 passing. people-chapter-identity, people-identity-seal, and people-generated-data internals were not supplied, and the forged-certificate test covers only the projection field. Production speedup is unmeasured. This grants no chapter, source, date, or live release approval.
